properties.description: Nafion composite with NiCu mixed metal oxide

nodes.name: NiCu precursor preparation
nodes.procedure: NiCu alloy and NiCu oxide were synthesized by mixing 10 mmol of nickel nitrate hexahydrate Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (97.0%, Sigma Aldrich) and 10 mmol Copper(II) sulfate pentahydrate (98.0%, Sigma Aldrich) in 500 ml water (18.2 MΩ·cm, 3 ppb TOC, Milli-Q ultrapure water). The precursor mixture was stirred for 15 min at 750 rpm.
nodes.source_text: NiCu alloy and NiCu oxide were synthesized by mixing 10 mmol of nickel nitrate hexahydrate... stirred for 15 min at 750 rpm.

nodes.name: NiCu chemical reduction
nodes.procedure: 200 ml of 0.15 M NaBH4 (98%, Sigma Aldrich) was added dropwise while bubbles were observed. The solution mixture was stirred for another 1 hour to ensure the complete chemical reduction of precursors. The resulting precipitate was centrifuged 5 times at 8000 rpm for 6 min and cleaned with water and ethanol three times. The produced precipitate was dried in a vacuum oven at 80°C overnight.

nodes.name: NiCu alloy annealing
nodes.procedure: The dried powder was annealed in 5% H2/Ar atmosphere at 500°C for 6 h with a ramping rate of 10°C/min.
nodes.source_text: The dried powder was annealed in... 5% H2/Ar to obtain NiCu alloy.

nodes.name: NiCu oxide annealing
nodes.procedure: The dried powder was annealed in an air atmosphere at 500°C for 6 h with a ramping rate of 10°C/min.
nodes.source_text: The dried powder was annealed in an air atmosphere to obtain NiCu oxide.

nodes.name: NiCu MMO carbonate precipitation
nodes.procedure: In order to make NiCu MMO, 100 ml of 1 M Na2CO3 (≥99.5%, Sigma-Aldrich) were added to nickel-copper precursors solution until the solution became milky and pH reached 10. The mixture was then stirred for another 15 min, followed by the addition of NaBH4 dropwise.
nodes.source_text: 100 ml of 1 M Na2CO3 were added to nickel-copper precursors solution until the solution became milky and pH reached 10. The mixture was then stirred for another 15 min, followed by the addition of NaBH4 dropwise.

nodes.name: NiCu MMO cleaning, drying and annealing
nodes.procedure: The produced catalyst was subjected to the same procedure for cleaning and drying as above. The dried powder was annealed in 5% H2/Ar atmosphere at 500°C for 6 h with a ramping rate of 10°C/min.

nodes.name: Carbon supported NiCu MMO synthesis
nodes.procedure: For catalyst supported on carbon, Ketjen black EC-600JD (AkzoNobel) was dispersed in the precursors' solution mixture to get (60 wt% catalyst supported on carbon) and stirred for another 1 hour before adding NaBH4 and complete the chemical reduction step [following the same cleaning, drying, and annealing procedure as NiCu MMO].

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCu MMO, NiCu alloy, and NiCu oxide catalysts exhibit agglomerated nanosheets morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM and STEM images of the nickel-copper catalyst... We investigated another nickel-copper catalyst without the addition of (NH4)2CO3... and they exhibited also an agglomerated nanosheets morphology similar to NiCu MMO as seen in (Fig. S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCu MMO nanosheets are loaded on carbon support (Ketjen black EC-600JD) with loosely stacked nanosheets morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The STEM image in Fig. 3c displays that NiCu MMO nanosheets are loaded on the carbon support (Ketjen black EC-600JD) with a dark thick region of NiCu nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX spectrum displays peaks corresponding to Ni, Cu, O, and C with Ni:Cu weight percentage as 52.3:47.7.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy dispersive x-ray spectroscopy (EDX) of NiCu MMO is shown in Fig. 4a. The EDX spectrum displays peaks corresponding to Ni, Cu, O, and C with Ni: Cu weight percentage as 52.3:47.7...

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCu MMO shows peaks corresponding to Ni (111) at 44.5°, Ni(200) at 51.93°, NiO (111) at 37.2°, NiO (200) at 43.2°, NiO (220) at 62.8°, and CuO at 32.5°, 35.6°, 38.9°, 48.9°.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD pattern of NiCu MMO in Fig. 4b shows peaks at 2θ values of 32.5°, 35.6°, 37.2°, 38.9°, 43.2°, 44.56°, 48.9°, 51.93°, and 62.8°. The diffraction peaks at 2θ values of 44.5° and 51.93° are associated with Ni (111) and Ni(200)... The peaks at 2θ values at 37.2°, 43.2°, and 62.8° correspond to (111), (200), and (220) diffraction planes of NiO... The diffraction peaks at 2θ values of 32.5°, 35.6°, 38.9°, 48.9° values correspond to CuO crystal structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCu MMO shows Raman peaks at 490, 606, 810, 1020, and 1100 cm⁻¹ corresponding to Cu(OH)₂, Bg Raman mode of CuO, and two-phonon NiO vibrational modes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectrum in Fig. 4c shows Raman peaks at 490, 606, 810, 1020, and 1100 cm⁻¹ respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCu MMO survey spectrum shows Ni, Cu, B, O, and C peaks. Ni 2p peaks indicate Ni⁰ at 853.8 eV and 871.4 eV, Ni²⁺ at 855.4 eV and 872.5 eV. Cu 2p peaks indicate Cu⁰ at 932.6 eV and 952.4 eV, CuO at 933.7 eV, and Cu(OH)₂ at 934.8 eV and 954.4 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS analysis provides sensitive information about the surface chemical composition of NiCu MMO catalyst. NiCu MMO survey spectrum is shown in Fig. 4d.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCu MMO possesses a surface area of 156 m²/g, NiCu alloy 112 m²/g, and NiCu oxide 92 m²/g.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The specific surface area of the NiCu catalysts was also investigated with Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) measurement... NiCu MMO possesses a surface area of 156 m²/g which is far higher than that of NiCu alloy (112 m²/g) and NiCu oxide (92 m²/g).
